entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: internal invariant violated: histogram subquery input is %T with %s sample kind
entries.rationale: the preceding lowerExpHistogramValuedShape call returned matched=true for the same inner expression selected by the histogram subquery recognizer. Every successful matched producer publishes SampleKindHistogram, so this split sample-kind half of the former row-shape assertion remains an internal invariant.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery step must be positive, got %s
entries.rationale: the PromQL parser rejects negative subquery steps; zero is the valid default handled before this guard

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: internal invariant violated: histogram subquery input matched no histogram-valued shape for %v
entries.rationale: selectFnOverExpHistogramSubquery admits this path only after isExpHistogramValuedShape recognizes the subquery inner. Re-dispatching that identical expression through the paired lowerExpHistogramValuedShape producer cannot return matched=false unless the internal recognizer and lowerer have drifted.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: histogram-valued subquery requires query eval-time context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: query handlers always supply evaluation context through LowerAt or LowerAtRange; only the raw test and tooling Lower entry can omit it, and selectFnOverExpHistogramSubquery's own subqueryHasEvalAnchor check already declines to match in that case — subqueryHasEvalAnchor is false exactly when subqueryGridCtx reports subqueryGridUnavailable, which is the state this guard tests — so this branch is unreachable even from that entry point
